## Status at a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Last updated** | YYYY-MM-DD |
| **What is happening now** | One sentence. |
| **Next step** | One sentence, with who does it and by when. |
| **Waiting on a person?** | No / Yes: who, for what, by when |
| **Outlook** | One sentence: will it finish on time, and why or why not. |

Status, priority, estimate and dates are in the project fields in the sidebar.

## Summary

Two to four sentences. What this work is and what will be different when it is finished. No technical terms.

## Why this matters

- **Who is affected:** which customers, staff or systems, and how many.
- **What it costs today:** money, time, risk, complaints. Use numbers and a time frame.
- **What happens if we do nothing:** the consequence, and how soon.
- **Why now:** what made this a priority.

## What "done" looks like

Statements a non-engineer could check for themselves.

- [ ] Outcome 1, written as something observable.
- [ ] Outcome 2.
- [ ] How we will confirm it worked after it goes live (what we measure, for how long).

## What is included and what is not

**Included:** the specific things this issue will do.
**Not included:** related things a reader might assume are covered, and where they are tracked instead (link the
issue).

## Approach

Three to six sentences in plain English describing how the work will be done and why this way. If options were
weighed, use the decision table:

| Option | What it means | Upside | Downside | Chosen? |
|--------|---------------|--------|----------|---------|
| A | | | | Yes, because… |
| B | | | | No, because… |

## Plan

- [ ] Step 1 in plain words
- [ ] Step 2
- [ ] Step 3

## Priority and effort: the reasoning

The current values are in the project fields. This section explains them.

- **Why this priority:** impact (who and how much) and urgency (what date makes it matter), in one or two sentences.
- **How the effort estimate was reached:** what the work consists of, what it was compared with, and what is and is
  not counted.
- **Range:** best case, most likely, worst case, and what would cause the worst case.
- **Human time needed:** who must spend time on this (review, decisions, testing) and roughly how many hours each.
- **Baseline:** the estimate and target date when the work was agreed, with the date. This line is never edited, so
  drift is visible later.

## Risks and unknowns

| Risk or unknown | How likely | What it would cost | What we are doing about it |
|-----------------|-----------|--------------------|----------------------------|
| | | | |

## Assumptions

Things taken as true without checking. Each one names who could confirm it.

## Who needs to be involved

- **Decision needed from:** name, the decision, the deadline.
- **Should be kept informed:** names or teams.

## Related work

- Part of: #parent
- Blocked by: #n (one line on what that issue delivers and why it is needed first)
- Blocks: #n
- Related: #n (one line on how)

## Glossary

Any term a reader might not know, each defined in one line.

---

## Technical details

For engineers. A non-technical reader can stop above this line.

- Where in the system: files, services, tables.
- Evidence: error messages, log excerpts (collapsed), measurements.
- Technical constraints and notes.
